function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick guide to help you find the perfect place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for a local bakery, a specialty shop, or a national delivery service. I’ve grouped the options by type and added a few handy tips for each.

---

## 1. Local & Artisan Bakeries  
*(Great for unique flavors, fresh ingredients, and supporting your community)*

| Bakery | Location | Specialty | Order Method | Notes |
|--------|----------|-----------|--------------|-------|
| **The Sweet Spot** | 123 Main St, Springfield | Classic French pastries & custom wedding cakes | Phone: (555) 123‑4567 or website: sweetspot.com | Known for their buttercream artistry; book 2–3 weeks ahead for large orders. |
| **Baker’s Dozen** | 45 Oak Ave, Brookfield | Gluten‑free & vegan options | Online form on bakersdozen.com | Offers a “build‑your‑own” cake kit for DIY celebrations. |
| **Cake & Co.** | 78 Maple Rd, Lakeside | Seasonal fruit tarts & artisanal chocolate | Email: orders@cakeandco.com | They accept custom designs via email; expect a 48‑hour turnaround. |
| **Patisserie Parisienne** | 12 Rue de la Gare, Downtown | French patisserie & macarons | Phone: (555) 987‑6543 | Their croquembouche is a showstopper for big events. |

> **Tip:** Call ahead to confirm availability, especially for custom designs or large orders. Many local shops offer free tastings if you’re planning a wedding or corporate event.

---

## 2. National Chains & Big‑Box Stores  
*(Convenient, often with nationwide delivery, and usually have a wide range of flavors)*

| Chain | Delivery Coverage | Typical Prices | Order Method | Highlights |
|-------|-------------------|----------------|--------------|------------|
| **Panera Bread** | Nationwide (via Panera’s online store) | $25–$60 per cake | Online: panera.com | Offers a “Panera Cake” line with seasonal flavors; free delivery in select cities. |
| **Dunkin’ Donuts** | Nationwide (via Dunkin’ app) | $20–$50 per cake | App or website: dunkindonuts.com | Known for their “Dunkin’ Cake” line; free delivery in many metro areas. |
| **Kraft Foods (Kraft Bakery)** | Nationwide (via Kraft.com) | $30–$70 per cake | Online: kraft.com | Offers a variety of pre‑made cakes and custom orders; free shipping on orders over $75. |
| **Walmart Grocery** | Nationwide (via Walmart.com) | $15–$40 per cake | Online: walmart.com | Great for budget orders; they have a “Cake & Pastry” section in most stores. |

> **Tip:** Check the chain’s website for “special occasion” promotions—many offer free delivery or a complimentary cupcake with a cake purchase.

---

## 3. Specialty & Gourmet Online Shops  
*(Perfect for high‑end events, themed parties, or when you want something truly unique)*

| Shop | Specialty | Delivery Areas | Order Method | Price Range |
|------|-----------|----------------|--------------|-------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Curated regional cakes from top U.S. bakeries | Nationwide (delivery times vary by region) | Online: goldbelly.com | $35–$120 per cake; includes a “delivery guarantee” for freshness. |
| **Martha & Sons** | Custom wedding cakes & luxury desserts | Nationwide (via their own delivery network) | Phone: (555) 321‑9876 or website: marthasons.com | $200–$500+ depending on size & design. |
| **Cake Concierge** | Bespoke cake design & 3‑D printing | Nationwide (via their own courier) | Online: cakeconcierge.com | $150–$400+; offers a “design consultation” video call. |
| **The Cake Shop** | Vegan & allergy‑friendly cakes | Nationwide (via their own delivery) | Online: thecakeshop.com | $25–$80 per cake; free shipping on orders over $100. |

> **Tip:** For gourmet orders, start at least 4–6 weeks in advance. These shops often require a deposit and have strict cancellation policies.

---

## 4. Food‑Delivery Platforms (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Postmates, etc.)  
*(Convenient if you already use a delivery app and want a quick pick‑up or same‑day delivery)*

| Platform | How it Works | Typical Delivery Fees | Best Use Cases |
|----------|--------------|-----------------------|----------------|
| **Uber Eats** | Search “cake” or “bakery” in the app | $3–$10 per delivery | Same‑day delivery from local bakeries; great for last‑minute gifts. |
| **DoorDash** | Browse “Desserts” or “Bakery” | $2–$8 per delivery | Ideal for picking up from a nearby shop while you’re out. |
| **Postmates** | Search “cake” or “dessert” | $4–$12 per delivery | Good for “just‑in‑time” deliveries; some shops offer “Postmates‑only” discounts. |

> **Tip:** Look for “delivery‑only” discounts or “first‑order” promos. Some platforms partner with specific bakeries for exclusive deals.

---

## 5. Tips for Ordering a Cake

1. **Plan Ahead** – For custom designs or large orders, give the bakery at least 2–3 weeks notice.  
2. **Confirm Delivery Times** – Ask whether the cake will be delivered “ready‑to‑eat” or if it needs to be refrigerated/kept at room temperature.  
3. **Ask About Tasting Options** – Many bakeries offer a tasting session for wedding cakes or corporate events.  
4. **Check Cancellation Policies** – Especially for custom orders; some bakeries require a non‑refundable deposit.  
5. **Read Reviews** – Look at recent customer feedback on Google, Yelp, or the bakery’s social media pages.  

---

### Quick Start Checklist

- [ ] Decide on the occasion (birthday, wedding, corporate event, etc.).  
- [ ] Choose a style: local artisan, national chain, or gourmet online.  
- [ ] Contact the bakery or visit their website to place an order.  
- [ ] Confirm the delivery date/time and any special instructions.  
- [ ] Pay the deposit (if required) and keep the receipt.  

Happy cake hunting! If you’d like me to look up a specific bakery in your city or compare prices for a particular flavor, just let me know.
